label: checker-b
statement: Reviewed only classifier-contract.md and the final checker-b-sample.json; no quarantine file was read. All 40 sampled transforms and 13 sampled analogs were reviewed; this is not an exhaustive analog review.

judgments.reason: Named seek, avoidance and separation weights change combined acceleration and observable unit paths.
Separation, cohesion and velocity weights change neighbour spacing and heading agreement within the flock.
Steering ranks and an acceleration threshold change the active motion group and its switching behaviour.
Slot spacing changes fixed target positions, formation width and measurable member-to-slot error.
Spacing, anchor speed and lag limit control moving slot targets and visible anchor-to-member distances.
Travel, danger and visibility costs change selected region costs, route choice and total route cost.
Source strength and radius reshape the terrain influence field and its controlled or contested areas.
The decay exponent and source strength change influence contours and the reach of terrain control.
A finite radius changes which terrain regions receive influence and where the field stops.
A tick delay directly changes notification arrival times and pending notification counts.
Slot spacing and moving-anchor speed change member trajectories, formation error and arrival spread.
Danger and exposure weights alter tactical route costs, producing visible route and risk changes.
The numeric selector threshold directly admits or drops complete unit messages at the channel.
Recipient count changes the numbered delivery set and the measurable number of message copies.
The next sequence value and finite buffer control which reordered messages leave consecutively.
Polling interval and batch limit change pickup times and how many queued messages arrive per turn.
Lease duration bounds notification delivery in time while subscriber count changes its recipient set.
The type count defines numbered matching routes, making type-based channel delivery observable.
Loop depth exposes the stated reciprocal creation path. A reviewer checking mutually defining ownership is a concrete correspondence.
Description level switches rule-step and whole-system views. A repairer escalating stalled local fixes to governing rules is a useful application.
Capture-to-display feedback supplies a real represented return path. Reviewer checks for monitoring output feeding its input match that loop.
Loop depth exposes the stated reciprocal creation path. Reviewer checks for mutually dependent foundations give a concrete application.
The three stated creator relations form a represented return path. Operator checks for circular approval authority correspond to that cycle.
Description level moves among dialogue, narrator and viewer views. The operator can similarly move stalled discussion to its enclosing goal.
Await-reply and in-flight limits change sender blocking, queued requests and reply-completion timing.
Batch size and flush interval change how command messages leave the queue and how long they wait.
Subscriber count and notification delay change actual notification recipients and arrival times.
One active input and completion-gated pending inputs preserve sequence. Executor and planner ordering of dependent mutations is a concrete counterpart.
The active-input limit changes concurrent routes and pending inputs. Executor and planner collection of bounded independent reports matches it.
First emission and the one-winner limit select one route and close losers. An operator choosing one responsive read-only provider is a concrete use.
The sampling period controls latest-message delivery ticks and latency. Cadenced operator status updates use the same practical selection rule.
Zero delay delivers in the sending step. Executor and verifier checks for callbacks finishing during startup address the same timing boundary.
The stated first-emission rule and one-winner limit select one delivery route and cancel the others.
The explicit adjacent-equality policy drops repeated payloads while delivering changed values.
The accepted numeric type code directly filters message deliveries and counts rejected types.
One in-flight delivery and drop-while-busy discard new arrivals until completion, visibly preventing overlapping submissions.
One in-flight delivery plus FIFO queues writes until completion and preserves their delivery order.
Window length and leading/trailing flags directly control immediate, suppressed and boundary deliveries.
The size parameter creates actual squad membership without claiming effectiveness. Operator and planner worker caps are a useful bounded analogy.
The per-tick quota changes admitted deliveries and queue depth. Operator and planner limits on request traffic give a concrete shared-capacity analogy.
